title: Choose the visual world for MDIP
question: The roll assigned the Mill Test Certificate. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Mill Test Certificate
options.lineage: EN 10204 3.1 inspection certificates that ship with every steel bar
options.thesis: Every prediction is issued like a material certificate: measured value, spec limit, verdict, stamp.
materials: security-paper ground with fine guilloche border
options.viewport: The landing page is one certificate sheet: header fields carry the nav and certificate number, the headline sits in the description field, and the primary action is a working 'submit your schedule for inspection' upload field; a task table shows planned vs forecast, risk and verdict, with a blue stamp certifying the real-data metrics.
options.risk: Can feel bureaucratic and dry if the table is set timidly; the stamp motif turns kitsch if used more than once per page.

raised.raise: The committed plan prints solid; every what-if scenario stays dashed until a supervisor signs it.
One dominant axis per page: the schedule timeline is the single long line every section hangs from.
Honest absence: a value the model cannot score shows as a labelled empty cell, never hidden, never zero.
One token source: landing and dashboard draw every colour, rule weight and type size from the same certificate set.
One cell grid: table columns, KPI fields and form fields share a single column rhythm.

options.label: Engineering Drawing Sheet
options.lineage: ISO technical drawings with zone borders, title block and revision table
options.thesis: The plan is a released drawing: zones, title block, revisions, and red clouds where the schedule changed.
materials: drafting sheet with A–F / 1–8 zone border
options.viewport: A drawing sheet with the product name in the title block bottom-right, navigation as zone references along the border, and the schedule drawn as a dimensioned timeline with revision clouds on slipping tasks.
options.risk: Familiar: 'technical drawing' is where many manufacturing sites land, so it can read as a blueprint costume.

options.label: Nixie Laboratory Counter
options.thesis: Every KPI is a bank of tubes with fixed digit places; a change in risk is a visible change of physical depth.
options.viewport: A steel panel of tube banks showing project risk, P50 slip and late tasks, digits cross-fading as a schedule is scored.
options.case: Holds product clarity for the numbers; loses audience identification, since planners do not live in lab instruments.
options.risk: Near-black with one glowing accent is one of the most common AI looks; dense tables have nowhere to live.

options.label: Sewing Pattern Envelope
options.lineage: home sewing pattern envelopes and tissue
options.thesis: Schedule variants as lettered views, the chosen one cut solid.
options.viewport: An envelope front indexing schedule views A, B, C.
options.case: Loses both axes: planners do not read their work as garment patterns.

options.label: Indoor Weather Sun
options.lineage: installation art: a mirrored hall with a half sun
options.thesis: One amber hall, navigated along its long axis.
options.viewport: A vast amber band with a half sun at the far wall.
options.case: Loses both axes: atmospheric art hides the numbers the product exists to show.
options.kept: One dominant long axis per page.

options.label: Ekiben Wrapper Kiosk
options.lineage: Japanese station bento wrappers with contents maps
options.thesis: Each project as a boxed meal with a true contents map.
options.viewport: A shelf of project boxes, one lid opened to its compartment map.
options.case: Loses both axes: the food-kiosk metaphor is foreign to a factory planning office.
options.kept: Honest absence: empty compartments stay visible.

options.label: Generative Parametric Identity
options.thesis: A parametric mark whose seed derives every token.
options.viewport: A live mark reseeding the whole page palette.
options.case: Loses both axes: a shifting identity fights the stable, trustworthy readout a plant needs.
options.kept: One token source drives every surface.

options.label: ANSI BBS Nightboard
options.thesis: The plant as a text-mode board of numbered screens.
options.viewport: A cyan title screen pouring in line by line over numbered menus.
options.case: Loses both axes: retro-terminal nostalgia, not shop-floor reality.
options.kept: Everything snaps to one strict cell grid.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean B2B SaaS site and dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and CTA beside a dashboard screenshot, feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
